ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is an outline map of Africa, with horizontal latitude reference lines drawn and six locations 1—6 marked. 1 is located in northeastern Africa, near the East African Plateau or Ethiopian Plateau; 2 is located near the low-latitude desert belt in the northwestern part of northern Africa; 3 is located in a lower-latitude area of inland West Africa; 4 is located in the inland area of south-central Africa; 5 is located near the southeastern coast of Africa; 6 is located on an island or nearshore area outside southeastern Africa. Reasoning: African natural zones as a whole have obvious latitudinal zonality, transitioning from tropical rainforest near the equator to tropical savanna and tropical desert to the north and south. 2, 3, 4, and 5 generally conform to this distribution pattern of natural zones controlled by latitude. Although the latitudinal position of 1 should correspond to an ordinary tropical natural zone, it is significantly affected by non-zonal factors such as the East African Plateau and high mountain terrain; 6 is located on a southeastern island or near the sea, and is obviously affected by land-sea position, ocean currents, sea winds, etc., deviating most strongly from simple latitudinal zonality. Therefore the places most strongly disturbed by non-zonal factors are 1 and 6.

raw_record.question_text:
Read the following figure and answer the following question.

<image1>

In the formation process of the six natural zones shown in the figure, which two places are most strongly disturbed by non-zonal factors?

method.method_draft: First describe the map: it is Africa with six labeled points and latitude reference lines. Locate each point by latitude and position. Establish the expected zonal natural-belt sequence for Africa from north to south. Compare the expected belt at each point’s latitude with the known/likely actual belt: points 2, 3, 4, and 5 generally fit the broad latitudinal sequence, whereas point 1 is strongly affected by East African plateau/highland conditions and point 6 by the southeast island/coastal oceanic-wind-current setting. Therefore select 1 and 6 as the two places with the greatest non-zonal interference.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：图中为非洲轮廓图，画有水平纬线参照线，标出1—6六个地点。1位于非洲东北部、东非高原或埃塞俄比亚高原附近；2位于非洲北部偏西的低纬沙漠带附近；3位于西非内陆较低纬地区；4位于非洲中南部内陆；5位于非洲东南部沿海附近；6位于非洲东南部外侧的岛屿或近海地区。推理：非洲自然带总体具有明显的纬度地带性，从赤道附近的热带雨林、向南北过渡到热带草原、热带荒漠等。2、3、4、5大体符合这种由纬度控制的自然带分布规律。1虽然纬度位置应对应普通热带自然带，但受东非高原、高山地形等非地带性因素影响显著；6位于东南岛屿或近海，受海陆位置、洋流、海风等影响明显，偏离单纯纬度地带性最强。因此受非地带性因素干扰最大的是1和6。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This route judges non-zonality by comparing each numbered place with the natural belt that should occur at the same latitude, so it relies on detecting the largest departures from latitudinal zonal patterns.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the Africa outline and the six numbered locations: 1 is in eastern Africa near the equatorial/tropical interior highlands, 6 is off or near the southeast side of Africa/Madagascar area, while 2–5 lie more regularly along the north-south latitudinal sequence shown by the horizontal latitude lines.
planner_metadata.text_role: Read that the question asks for the two of the six shown natural belts whose formation is most disturbed by non-zonal factors.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use the rule that natural belts normally show latitudinal zonality controlled mainly by heat and moisture, but large deviations at the same latitude indicate non-zonal controls such as terrain uplift, ocean currents, monsoon/trade-wind exposure, or island/coastal effects. East African highlands and Madagascar/southeast coastal areas are classic non-zonal exceptions in Africa.

method.method_draft: Inspect the positions of the six labels and screen them for major non-zonal controls. Mark point 1 because its eastern African highland location means altitude and terrain dominate over simple latitude. Mark point 6 because its southeast island/coastal position means ocean current, prevailing winds, and maritime exposure strongly modify moisture and vegetation. Treat points 2–5 as mainly controlled by latitude/large-scale zonal climate belts. Conclude that the maximum non-zonal disturbance occurs at points 1 and 6.
